alternatives_considered.approach: Drive the activity filter with the client SegmentedControl island instead of the server GET chip form.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The filter must live in the URL so it survives reload, shared links and the retry after a failed load; the GET form works before JavaScript arrives and already carries the sibling expense filter through hidden inputs, which a client control would have to reimplement.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep updateProfile's redirect-on-refusal and preserve failed profile input with a sessionStorage draft restore in the new island.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It preserves a transport that contradicts the house rule (conventions.md: refusals go inline; redirects are for success) and trades a documented pattern for per-page storage cleverness; the inline refusal keeps the typed state naturally because the form never unmounts.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add feed pagination with a load-more button to satisfy 'failed pages show load-more retry' literally.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The contract face of this issue fixes the activity reads as unchanged, and paging would change the readers both feeds share; the existing section-level retry with the filter preserved is what 'failed pages' maps to without touching the reads.

alternatives_considered.approach: Put the viewer-zone timestamp and its formatter in a new components/timestamp.tsx plus lib/dates/format.ts.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: One caller does not earn two modules; components/ui-interactive.tsx is already the shared home for stateful presentational pieces and its pure helpers are already unit-tested from app/ui-set.test.ts, so the island and its formatter belong there.

alternatives_considered.approach: Key the members roster avatars on displayName so roster and feed tints always agree.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would break the shared set's documented contract (same member, same colour on every screen and render) and the app/ui-set.test.ts pin that renaming must not recolour; the feed can only be name-keyed because ActivityRow carries no actor id, so the mismatch is disclosed instead of spreading it to the roster.

work_order.approach: Restyle the three screens onto the shared set that piece 1 already merged (Button, Card, Avatar, Badge, TextInput, Skeleton, EmptyState, ConfirmStep, Dialog patterns, design tokens) without touching any read or write logic: the members roster becomes composed avatar rows (not ListRow, which cannot hold a badge cluster plus an inline form inside an anchor) with words-plus-colour balances from a new directionWords helper and owner actions behind a no-JS details disclosure; the invite panel keeps its copy island and single-notice confirm flow; the activity feed keeps its URL-chip GET form with hidden preserved inputs and exact-changed-fields edit detail, owns its EmptyState through the unchanged emptyText string plus an optional action, and gains a viewer-zone Timestamp island; profile becomes one card with a controlled island whose refusals go inline per ADR-0008 and conventions while success keeps the ?saved=1 redirect. The balance-blocked predicate and its sentence live in client-safe lib/groups/validation.ts with NonZeroBalanceError built from the same constant so the sentence cannot drift; no client island imports the drizzle-backed members module. Server text for rotation failure, balance-blocked removal and claim-taken stays byte-identical; only its presentation changes, plus a settle-up link beside balance-blocked refusals and a legacy reader for ?error=invalid so the pinned selector surface keeps rendering.
assumptions: Piece for #33 (or the #40 foundation work on main) has merged the shared set, AppShell, tokens and Inter/lucide-react this plan builds on; no new design-system component or token is introduced — ProfileForm, CopyLinkButton and the Timestamp island are app-level compositions over the existing set.

The contract face fixes reads and actions, so listMembers, listGroupActivity, listUserActivity, computeNetBalances and all group/auth actions keep their signatures, schemas, messages and success transports; the single exception is updateProfile's failure transport, which moves from redirect to the inline-refusal state the house rule (ADR-0008, conventions.md) already prescribes for refusals — a presentation transport, not a rule change.

With no actor id on ActivityRow the feed avatar tint can only derive from the actor name while the roster stays id-keyed per the avatar contract, so the same person may tint differently between roster and feed and a rename recolours their feed avatar; the roster is deliberately not re-keyed.

'Failed pages show load-more retry' (IAC-4, ui.md Activity partial) is read as 'a failed feed read shows its retry': the cross-group error card with the filter preserved plus the group excerpt's section retry; no pagination is added because the reads are fixed.

Timestamps are stored UTC and the viewer zone is only knowable on the client, so the server renders a UTC-labelled fallback and the island replaces it in an effect (never during render), falling back to the UTC label when the time zone is unavailable and clamping future values instead of printing 'in 3 hours'.
PGlite serves one connection, so the sequential withDb reads stay sequential; no read is parallelised.
sdlc:verify here is typecheck plus test:ci plus build; the work-order lint step does not apply because the repo has no lint script by decision.

The members loading fallback markers (#invite-url, notice params, data-skeleton names, bg-muted/20 with motion-safe:animate-pulse, aria-busy) stay stable because qa/selectors.md and the loading test pin them.
lib/auth/actions.test.ts pins updateProfile redirecting on invalid input and will be updated to the inline-refusal contract in this change.
work_order.confidence_rationale: Every function to change has been read, every caller of the shared pieces is listed in the file reasons, and the critique's one genuine bundle-layer defect (drizzle pulled into the client) is designed out by hoisting the predicate into validation.ts; the remaining risk is QA selector churn on the profile error path plus the disclosed avatar-tint mismatch, both flagged rather than hidden. What would move the number down is discovering a second client import of a db-backed module; what would move it up is a passing preflight plus the pinned loading/marker tests staying green.
work_order.debate_summary: The critique was right three times and manufacturing noise twice. Accepted outright: (1) the isBalanceBlockedRefusal bundle defect — value-importing lib/groups/members.ts from a 'use client' island would drag drizzle-orm and the db schema into the browser bundle, so the predicate and sentence now live in client-safe validation.ts with NonZeroBalanceError built from the same constant; (2) the double-owned empty state — EmptyState now has one owner (inside ActivityFeed behind the unchanged emptyText string, new props optional so the group excerpt inherits without an edit); (3) the Card/panel double-h2 — Cards wrap without titles and keep the panels' aria-labelledby h2s. Accepted as disclosure, rejected as a change: the name-keyed feed avatars cannot match the id-keyed roster (ActivityRow carries no actor id and the contract face forbids adding one), so the mismatch is stated in assumptions and the roster is deliberately not re-keyed. Rejected: the blocking demand to escalate the profile transport — redirect-on-refusal contradicts the binding house rule that refusals go inline (ADR-0008, conventions.md) and ui.md's 'failed saves never clear input', while schemas, messages and both success redirects stay byte-identical, so the transport move is inside the ticket, not an amendment of it; the sessionStorage-restore alternative stays rejected. Minor findings (ListRow fit, directionWords helper, styled select, load-more interpretation, assumption wording) were all folded into the work order, and the load-bearing edge cases (archived/disabled invite gating, viewer-perspective wording, hydration/timezone/future-time behaviour, pending guard after refusal, pinned skeleton/notice/selector markers, filtered-vs-truly-empty) are now explicit file constraints or acceptance text.

qa_script: Boot the branch build and sign up two users A (owner) and B, plus create a group with expenses, a payment and a placeholder seat.

As A at /groups/<id>/members at 375px and 1280px: roster shows avatars, You/Owner/Placeholder badges, balances in words plus colour, keyboard opens the row overflow disclosure and Remove confirms by naming the member.
Invite panel: copy the link via #invite-url, rotate behind its confirm (new link works, notice shows), disable behind its confirm, then create a fresh link.
Blocked removal: attempt to remove a member with a nonzero balance, read the refusal naming the blocker with a settle-up link; settle up, then remove successfully and read the single status notice.
Claim flow: as B open the invite link, claim the matching placeholder seat, land in the group; open the same seat link again in a second tab and read the taken notice.

Activity at /activity and the group excerpt: all four chips filter correctly, timestamps read relative-then-human in the local zone, expense-edited entries show exactly the changed fields, empty group feed explains itself, filtered-empty keeps its own sentence, failed load keeps the filter on retry.

Profile at /profile: save a new name and currency and read the saved notice; submit an empty name and confirm the input is kept with an inline error; confirm no sign-out control on the page and sign-out works from the account menu by keyboard at 375px.
Keyboard and contrast pass at both widths over all three screens, including the chip row, disclosure, dialogs and the styled currency select; reduced-motion shows no animation.
residual_risks: The group page excerpt inherits the feed redesign without its owning ticket reviewing it; visually intended, but its QA belongs to the sibling piece.
The details-based overflow disclosure is keyboard-accessible without JavaScript but is not a true ARIA menu; a strict menu-pattern review may ask for a menu island later.

Two identically named placeholder seats are matched by name in the claim flow (existing logic, untouched here): one person must not be able to claim both, and the roster must not read them as one person — flagged for the owning ticket's QA.
risks: Moving the profile failure from ?error=invalid to inline state changes the QA walk pinned in selectors.md; the page keeps rendering ?error=invalid for direct hits and ?saved=1 is untouched, but the replay walk for a failed save must assert the inline node instead.
updateProfile becomes an island-style (previous, formData) action; any caller outside the profile form would need the same update, and the grep shows only the profile page and its tests call it.
Payment rows render amounts in neutral ink with from-to words; if reviewers expect lent/owed colouring on payments, that is a one-line tone decision inside ActivityRowItem.
Client islands in this change may only import client-safe modules (validation, money/format, ui); the db-backed members module stays server-only, which the validation.ts hoist enforces structurally.

issue_snapshot.title: Members, activity and profile plus display and accessibility sweep
issue_snapshot.body:
Inviting, rostering, following what changed, and editing a profile all look like the same product, with money, dates, and states reading consistently everywhere.

UI face: owner manages roster and invites, everyone reads a filterable human-dated activity feed, and the user edits name plus default currency on one card, with consistent money, date, and state treatment everywhere. Contract face: consumes shell, rows, avatars, badges, dialogs, and skeletons from piece 1; uses the existing membership, invite, activity, and profile reads and actions unchanged. Follows docs/ui.md Members and invite, Activity, and Profile structures plus the Money display, Errors, Skeletons, Empty states, and Accessibility patterns exactly.

**Out of scope**
- Any membership, invite-token, activity-writing, or profile logic change
- Landing, home, group, expense, and settle-up screens (sibling pieces)
- Dark mode, which ui.md explicitly defers

Covers: TR-11, S-8
Part of #31.
Depends on #33.

## Acceptance (from the split)
- **IAC-1** MEMBERS: roster rows show avatar, name, You, Owner, and Placeholder badges with per-member balance in words plus colour, overflow menus for owner actions, and an invite-link panel with copy button, disable and rotate behind confirms.
- **IAC-2** MEMBERS: claiming a matching placeholder on join prompts correctly; empty group prompts sharing the invite link with a copy button; invite rotation failure keeps the old link active and says so; balance-blocked removal names the blocker and points at settle-up.
- **IAC-3** ACTIVITY: feed shows chronological rows with actor avatar, plain-sentence action, relative-then-human timestamp in the viewer zone, and link-through; filter segmented control or scroll chip row covers all, expenses, payments, and members; expense-edited entries summarise exactly the changed fields.
- **IAC-4** ACTIVITY: empty feed explains it fills as the group acts; loading shows skeleton event rows; failed pages show load-more retry; feed error shows retry with filter selection preserved.
- **IAC-5** PROFILE: single settings card shows display name and styled default-currency select with Save and pending guard; sign-out lives in the account menu, never as a red button; failed save keeps input and offers retry.
- **IAC-6** GLOBAL SWEEP: zero balances are neutral everywhere, direction is always words plus colour, dates read as people say them with times in the viewer zone, and every screen in this piece has designed empty, loading, and error states at 375px and 1280px meeting the ui.md accessibility rules and checklists.

Record the redesign as a new ADR.
